title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
slides: Is Mark Zuckerberg about to replace your assistant?
Meta plans agents that act on your behalf
But these AI agents know your private data
You can offload decisions you hate making
Test one small task delegation by next week
thread_text:
1. Is your data already exposed?

Meta wants AI agents that act for you. That means your private messages, preferences, and habits will be fed directly into those bots.

2. They call it "proactive assistance"

You won't even ask for help — the agent will decide when to step in. And it will have access to every message and calendar entry you’ve ever shared.

3. You can offload decisions you hate

Let the agent choose your restaurant or book your dentist. But every choice it makes is stored and analyzed — forever.

4. Privacy is the trade-off you never see

To act like you, the agent needs to be you. That means reading your DMs, your emails, your location history.

5. Test one small task delegation by next week

Hand over a single decision — like scheduling a coffee meeting — to an AI. Did it save you time? Or did you spend more fixing it?
video_script: Meta's AI agents want your private data.
They'll act for you without being asked.
You can offload boring decisions to them.
But they must read all your messages.
Try delegating one small task this week.

instagram.caption:
Meta wants AI agents that read your private messages, calendar, and location to act on your behalf — without you even asking.

These bots are designed to offload decisions you hate, like booking appointments or choosing restaurants. But every choice they make is stored and analyzed forever.

For content creators: your private DMs, emails, and habits will train a bot that mimics your judgment — then hands those insights to Meta's servers.

What one small task would you let an AI decide this week — and what data are you trading for that convenience? 🤖🔍💬
